name: Harbona
title: Eunuch at the court of King Ahasuerus
summary: Harbona was one of the seven eunuchs (court officials) who served King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) in Persia. He is best known for his crucial intervention during Haman's downfall, when he drew the king's attention to the gallows Haman had built to hang Mordecai. His single remark changed the course of events and contributed to Haman being hanged on his own gallows.

keyEvents.title: One of the king's seven eunuchs
keyEvents.description: Harbona is mentioned as one of the seven court officials who served directly under King Ahasuerus and had access to the king's presence.

keyEvents.title: Sent to bring Queen Vashti
keyEvents.description: King Ahasuerus sent Harbona along with the other six eunuchs to fetch Queen Vashti to a banquet, which led to her removal when she refused to come.

keyEvents.title: Reveals Haman's gallows
keyEvents.description: At the decisive moment when the king's anger was directed at Haman, Harbona informed the king that Haman had built a gallows fifty cubits high to hang Mordecai, who had saved the king's life.

keyEvents.title: Haman's Downfall Sealed
keyEvents.description: Harbona's suggestion about the gallows led the king to order that Haman himself be hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. This was a turning point in the story of the book of Esther.

keyEvents.title: God's Providence Through a Court Official
keyEvents.description: Harbona served as an instrument of God's providence. His seemingly simple remark about the gallows was part of the divine plan to save the Jewish people from Haman's extermination plot.
